Vandegrift commanded the 1st Marine Division from the 7 August 1942 landing until relieved by Patch on 9 December 1942 (Miller, ch. III and IX; Zimmerman; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9).

Patch is named as commanding general of the Americal Division on 9 December 1942, when he assumed command of troops ashore, and was succeeded in that division command by Sebree when XIV Corps was activated on 2 January 1943 (Miller, ch. IX). valid_from is the first date he is named in this increment, not a sourced appointment day as Americal commander.
Sebree succeeded Patch as commander of the Americal Division when XIV Corps was activated on 2 January 1943 (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). End left open in this increment.
Patch became commanding general of XIV Corps when Harmon activated the corps on 2 January 1943 (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). End left open in this increment.

Collins is named as commanding general of the 25th Infantry Division on the first claim of the landing (17 December 1942) and again on 10 January 1943 (Miller, ch. IX and XI). valid_from is the first date he is named in this increment, not a sourced appointment day. End left open.

De Carre acted as commanding general of the 2nd Marine Division on Guadalcanal; Marston remained in New Zealand because he was senior to Patch (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9). End left open in this increment.

Hyakutake is named as commanding general of 17th Army in Miller, chapters IV–VII, and in the JACAR 17th Army record. valid_from is the first on-island claim in this increment (mid-October), not a sourced appointment day. End left open.
Ichiki commanded the detachment from the 18 August landing until it was destroyed at the Ilu on 21 August 1942 (Miller, ch. IV).

Kawaguchi commanded the 35th Infantry Brigade / Kawaguchi Force from the 29 August–11 September landings (Miller, ch. V). End left open in this increment (he was later relieved; a dated relief was not copied from a page read).
Miller, chapter V, names Col. Akinosuka Oka as commander of the 124th Infantry, nucleus of the Kawaguchi Force. End left open.
Maruyama commanded the 2nd Division in the October counter-offensive (Miller, ch. VI). valid_from is the mid-October assembly claim. End left open.

Sumiyoshi commanded the 17th Army artillery and the Matanikau coast force in the October counter-offensive (Miller, ch. VI). valid_from is the 23 October attack claim, not a sourced appointment day. End left open.

Nasu commanded the left wing in the 24–26 October assaults (Miller, ch. VI). valid_to is the last claim of the force in this increment (the night of 25–26 October). Miller lists him among the dead of the counter-offensive but does not give the day of death; that day is not invented here.

Miller, ch. V, and Zimmerman, ch. VI: Edson took command of the 5th Marines on 21 September 1942 after Colonel Hunt’s departure. The last claim in this increment that names him is 3 November (Point Cruz pocket). The 5th Marines sailed on 9 December (C12796) but that row does not name him, so the tenure is left open at the last named claim.

Arrived with the 1st MAW command echelon on 3 September 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Part VI, ch. 5 and Appendix C). Appendix C lists him as Major General, the highest rank held in the period; the arrival narrative calls him Brigadier General. Rank on the tenure is the arrival rank. Tenure left open at the last claim in this increment.
Appendix C: CO of MAG-23 20 August–4 November 1942.
Commanded VMF-223 for its Guadalcanal period 20 August–16 October 1942.
Commanded VMSB-232 for its Guadalcanal period 20 August–2 November 1942.
Commanded VMF-224 at Henderson Field 30 August–2 November 1942.

Led the first five P-400s of the 67th Fighter Squadron into Henderson Field on 22 August 1942. The 27 August increment was flown in by Captain John A. Thompson; this tenure is only the 22 August arrival, not a claim that Brannon commanded the squadron after that day. (Brannon later appears on 12 November with the 339th.)

Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2: Major Dale D. Brannon brought eight P-38s of the 339th Fighter Squadron into Henderson Field on 12 November 1942. No later commander is named in the chapters read; tenure left open at that claim.
Commanded the 11th Bombardment Group at Espiritu Santo in the chapters read (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 2). Tenure dated from the first copied claim (6 August 1942) and left open.
First commander of Thirteenth Air Force, headquarters on Espiritu Santo from the activation on 13 January 1943 (Craven and Cate, vol. IV, ch. 3).
Commanded the 2nd MAW forward echelon from 26 December 1942 (USMC Operations vol. I, Appendix C).

Appendix C: CO of MAG-14 from 16 October 1942 to 17 December 1942, then Colonel William O. Brice. No 17 December claim is entered in this increment (no location is copied for that command-change day), so the tenure end is dated from the appendix only and is not linked to an asserts_end claim.
Named in command of TF 61 on 24 August 1942 (Cressman). Tenure dated to the sourced battle day only; earlier or later command of the combined force is not entered from a numbered source.
Named in command of TF 16 on 26 October and 13 November 1942 (Cressman). The end is the last sourced day in this increment, not a documented relief.
Named in command of TF 17 at Santa Cruz, 26 October 1942 (Cressman). Extended through 27 October, when Hornet was sunk, as the continuance of the same battle (annotated).
Named in command of TF 18 when Wasp was torpedoed, 15 September 1942 (Cressman). Tenure dates are the sourced 15 September battle day only, not a documented relief (end is the last sourced day).
Named in command of TF 18 at Rennell Island, 29-30 January 1943 (Cressman).
Named in command of TG 64.2 at Cape Esperance, 11-12 October 1942 (Cressman).

Named in command of TG 67.4 in the Cruiser Night Action; killed 13 November 1942 (Cressman). Tenure start and end are the 13 November night action as Cressman files it (the fighting began late on the 12th); Callaghan was killed on board San Francisco that night.
Named in command of TF 64, 14-15 November 1942 (Cressman).

Named in command of TF 67 unloading in Lunga Roads, 12 November 1942 (Cressman). Tenure dates are the sourced 12 November day only, not a documented relief; Wright's later tenure on the same task force is a separate increment of command.
Named in command of TF 67 at Tassafaronga, 30 November 1942 (Cressman; ONI). Extended through 1 December for the sinking of Northampton, a consequence of the same action (annotated).
Named in command of the Savo cruiser force, flag in Chokai, on 9 August 1942 (Cressman; USSBS). Dated to the sourced battle day only.

Named in command of the Cape Esperance covering force, flag in Aoba, and killed on board Aoba (Cressman, 11 October). Dated to the sourced battle night as Cressman files it (the action began shortly before midnight on the 11th).
Named in command of the bombardment force in the Cruiser Night Action (Cressman; USSBS). Dated to 13 November as Cressman files the night action.
Named in command of the 15 November night force, flag in Atago (Cressman; USSBS). Dated to the sourced battle day only.

Named 司令長官 中将 三川軍一 on the 人員ノ現状 table of the 8th Fleet wartime log for 14 July–31 August 1942 (C08030022500, PDF p. 23). Tenure is dated to that monthly diary only; later monthly 人員 pages were not used to extend it in this increment.

Monzen (門前大佐) is named as commander of the 11th Construction Unit on 7 August 1942 in JACAR C25080307000 p. 2 (stamp 1308). valid_from is that claim date, not a sourced appointment day. End left open; a later departure day was not read.

Named Teishin Attack Force commander on the JACAR bombardment record (C08030723100) and as Rear Admiral Kurita Takeo in command of the Haruna and Kongo bombardment force in Cressman on 14 October. Tenure is dated to the night of the bombardment only (JACAR opens fire at 2226 on 13 October; Cressman records the PT action under 14 October).
Named Support Force commander on the JACAR order issued at Shortland, flagship Suzuya, on 11 November 1942 (C08030768500). Dated to that sourced day only. A rank is not on the order page.
